raw.description:
About Karbon

Karbon is the global leader in AI-powered practice management software for accounting firms. We provide an award-winning cloud platform that helps tens of thousands of accounting professionals work more efficiently and collaboratively every day. With customers in 40 countries, we have grown into a globally distributed team across the US, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the Philippines. We are well-funded, ranked #1 on G2, growing rapidly, and have a people-first culture that is recognized with Great Place To Work® certification and on Fortune magazine's Best Small Workplaces™ List.

We are hiring a Senior Manager of Revenue Operations Systems to lead the team that owns Salesforce across Sales, Marketing, and the Customer organization, and to own the technology stack that powers our sales team. This person sets the architecture and standards for our core GTM platform, runs the team's intake and allocation, and makes sure every tool we pay for earns its place.

This is a player-coach role. Expect roughly half your time building: designing solutions, shipping complex configuration, and reviewing the architecture your team delivers. The other half goes to leading a team of three Revenue Operations Analysts, managing the team's workload, and partnering with GTM leaders so the right work gets done in the right order. We are looking for someone who is the most capable technical operator in the room and gets real energy from making the people around them better. As the function grows, so will the scope of this role.

Karbon is building an agentic organization. Every role here is expected to operate with an AI-first mindset, and this role carries a specific expectation: grow your team's capacity faster than its headcount. The rest of this JD describes what that looks like for Salesforce and the sales technology stack.

About the Role

Salesforce Platform Leadership

  • Own Salesforce as the core GTM platform for Sales, Marketing, and the Customer organization, including the data model, lifecycle automation, sharing and security model, and release management. Set the platform standards and architecture principles your team builds to
  • Design and ship solutions end to end, from complex flows and record types to integrations. Review and approve architectural changes from your team and others, and hold a high bar on quality, documentation, and change management
  • Architect how Salesforce connects to the rest of the GTM stack. Own integration patterns (native, middleware, event-driven) and know when to use each. Build with observability in mind so issues are caught before the business feels them
  • Partner with the Senior Manager of Marketing Operations on the data flow between marketing systems and Salesforce, including campaign sync, lead and contact routing, and attribution field architecture

Sales Technology Stack

  • Own the sales technology stack, including sales engagement, conversation intelligence, data enrichment, and quoting tools, along with the integrations that connect them to Salesforce. Run vendor evaluations, implementations, renewals, and consolidation analyses
  • Keep technology aligned to how Sales, Marketing, and the Customer organization work. Stay close enough to each team to understand their workflows, translate their needs into the right systems decisions, and say no when a new tool is not the answer
  • Make build vs. buy vs. automate decisions with business-case rigor. Identify redundancies, integration gaps, and where AI can remove manual work across the stack. The expectation is to continuously improve how the sales organization is enabled by technology, not just maintain what we have
  • Maintain the tech stack inventory, ownership, and renewal calendar for your domain so leadership and Finance always know what we use, what it costs, who owns it, and what it returns

Data Quality & Governance

  • Own data governance for the Salesforce platform: field definitions and ownership, stage gate enforcement, validation, and dashboard accuracy. Every field has a definition and an owner, and the numbers leaders see can be trusted
  • Run the change management and release process that keeps Salesforce stable as it scales. Enforce scope and intake boundaries without needing escalation
  • Surface issues before they are reported. Connect symptoms to root causes across systems, and frame findings in terms of revenue impact and a proposed action

Team Leadership & Workload Management

  • Lead and develop a team of three Revenue Operations Analysts: two focused on Salesforce and connected tools, and one supporting the Customer organization (customer success, service delivery, and support). Coach through weekly 1:1s and semi-annual reviews, build development plans tailored to each person, and grow people into bigger scope
  • Own the performance process for your team: goal setting, mid-year and annual reviews, calibration, and merit and promotion cases. Address underperformance early and directly
  • Own intake, prioritization, and allocation for the team. Publish the queue, manage to defined SLAs, and make the Now/Next/Later call with the Director of Revenue Operations as a partner. Push back on low-ROI work and reallocate toward the highest-leverage activity
  • Run capacity planning for your team. Every headcount ask is justified through the agentic lens: what AI has already taken on, what still needs a person, and why. Design AI-augmented workflows as the default for new work and teach your team to do the same
  • Own hiring for your team as roles open: write the JD, run the interview loop, and build onboarding that gets new hires productive quickly
  • Codify tribal knowledge into documented processes and runbooks. Remove single points of failure on the team, including yourself

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Be a trusted partner to Sales, Marketing, and Customer leaders at the Director and VP level. Translate their questions into the systems and data changes that answer them, and communicate in business terms
  • Own the roadmap for Salesforce and the sales technology stack, and sequence it against the GTM plan. Present priorities and progress to GTM leadership monthly
  • Lead multi-quarter, cross-functional initiatives end to end. Keep stakeholders informed before they have to ask, and never surprise anyone on delivery

About You!

  • 8+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or Salesforce administration in a B2B SaaS environment, including at least 2 years leading a team. You are as comfortable building a complex flow yourself as you are walking the CRO through the roadmap
  • Deep Salesforce expertise. You have personally built and scaled Salesforce at a growing company and understand the architecture beneath the UI: data model, sharing and security, automation, APIs, and release management. Experience supporting post-sale teams in Salesforce is a strong plus
  • Cross-platform breadth. You have owned Salesforce alongside at least three integrated GTM platforms (e.g., sales engagement, conversation intelligence, marketing automation, data enrichment, CPQ) and can speak to how data moves between them
  • A track record of owning a tech stack. You have run evaluations, implementations, renewals, and consolidations, and can point to tools you added, tools you cut, and why
  • A people leader who grows people. You have coached analysts or admins into bigger scope, handled hard performance conversations with clarity, and managed a shared queue with competing priorities from multiple teams
  • Revenue literacy. You understand the full revenue engine, from new business to expansion, retention, and churn, and you prioritize by revenue impact. You can defend why one request matters more than another in terms a revenue leader accepts
  • Operational rigor with architectural thinking. You balance urgency in fixing what is broken today with a clear vision for what the system needs to look like at 2x and 5x scale
  • An AI-first operator. You are using AI in your work today, you have shipped AI-assisted workflows that expanded real capacity, and you have a point of view on how AI reshapes Revenue Operations
  • Clear, direct communicator. Tight for executives, detailed for peers, and willing to push back when the work calls for it
  • Experience in accounting, professional services, or practice management software is a plus but not required

Why Work at Karbon?

  • Industry-leading benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and up to three eligible dependents. Also:
    • Work-from-home allowance
    • Rice subsidy
    • Meal allowance per working day
    • Laundry allowance
  • 15 paid time off days per year (which includes 5 Karbon Days per year)
  • 7 Sick leave days per year
  • Internet and work-from-home subsidy
  • Discretionary bonus program
  • Work with (and learn from) a very experienced team
  • Be part of a startup team that will continue to grow around you
  • Flexible approach to work environment (we believe in trust and autonomy)
  • A culture of open communication, consistent feedback, and full transparency into company results, metrics, and financial position

Please be aware that Karbon will only contact you via email from our domain, karbonhq.com. If you receive an email from any other domain, please do not click any of those links.

Research has shown that women and underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single criteria. Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Director, Customer Experience, Partner Program in our strategic partner services organization, you will be tasked with defining how SentinelOne governs the services delivered with our partners, owning the end-to-end service catalog, clear definitions of service scope, and the SLA, SLO, and experience-level (XLA) framework across delivery towers. This role turns a complex partnership, which brings together SentinelOne's AI-powered security platform and our partners' expertise in managed detection and response, managed SIEM, and incident response, into an operating model with clear commitments, escalation procedures, accountabilities, and verifiable customer outcomes. You will lead through standards, data, and cross-functional collaboration rather than through direct management of partner delivery staff.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Own and maintain the joint service catalog, including service definitions, boundaries, inclusions, exclusions, prerequisites, and operational ownership.
  • Define and govern SLA, service-level objective (SLO), and XLA measurement standards for Threat Services, Professional Services, and related offerings.
  • Establish service-management processes for intake, incident and problem management, change control, escalation, continuous improvement, and service transition.
  • Collaborate with the partner's service-delivery leadership to align operational handoffs, RACI, review cadence, and decision mechanisms.
  • Translate customer and contractual commitments into measurable service requirements, quality thresholds, and audit-ready evidence.
  • Chair service-management reviews and track cross-tower issues through documented corrective actions.
  • Set expectations for capacity planning, service readiness, exceptions, reporting controls, and escalation thresholds.
  • Partner with independent performance and analytics teams to ensure service measures are consistently defined and traceable to evidence.
  • Lead, develop, and prioritize the SentinelOne service-management capability as the program scales.
  • Deliver against success measures including a current, adopted service catalog with clear accountable owners and delivery boundaries; reliable aggregate SLA, SLO, and XLA attainment and fewer unresolved ownership gaps; service governance adopted across customer, partner, product, and commercial stakeholders; recurring service failures addressed through measurable remediation; and better customer experience without unnecessary executive escalation.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

  • 10 or more years of experience in enterprise service delivery, IT service management, managed security services, or service operations, including people leadership.
  • Proven ability to design service catalogs, operating models, SLAs, SLOs, XLAs, and service-review governance.
  • Strong experience with partner or outsourced delivery contracts, service boundaries, and multi-party escalation management.
  • Working knowledge of ITIL disciplines, service assurance, problem management, and continual service improvement.
  • Strong operational and analytical skills, with the ability to link service definitions with telemetry, commercial commitments, and customer outcomes.
  • Effective executive communication, negotiation, documentation, and decision-making across matrixed teams.
  • Ability to lead a team and influence senior stakeholders while managing conflicting service priorities.
  • Experience in cybersecurity MDR, managed SIEM, incident response, or technical professional services.
  • Experience building a service function during a large provider transition or partnership launch.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. T-Rex is seeking an experienced Microsoft Transformation Architect to lead enterprise modernization across the Microsoft ecosystem for our FSA customer. The architect will define the target-state architecture and transformation roadmap spanning Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Entra identity, Windows, and security platforms, guiding the agency from legacy environments to secure, integrated, cloud-enabled services that meet federal compliance requirements.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop the enterprise target-state architecture, transformation roadmap, and business case across Azure, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Windows platforms.
  • Assess the current application, infrastructure, identity, and collaboration landscape, and define migration waves and dependencies.
  • Architect Azure and Azure Government landing zones, hybrid connectivity, and workload migrations for Windows and Linux applications.
  • Lead Microsoft 365 modernization, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, and tenant-to-tenant or on-premises migrations.
  • Design identity modernization with Active Directory consolidation, Microsoft Entra ID, conditional access, and Zero Trust principles.
  • Design endpoint modernization using Windows 11, Microsoft Intune, Autopilot, and Azure Virtual Desktop.
  • Integrate Microsoft Defender, Purview, and Sentinel to meet DISA STIG, NIST SP 800-53, FISMA, FedRAMP, and agency ATO requirements.
  • Automate deployment and governance using PowerShell, Bicep, Terraform, and Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions.
  • Produce architecture artifacts and executive briefings for government stakeholders and architecture review boards, and mentor engineering teams in an Agile delivery environment.

Requirements:

  • 10+ years of IT experience, including 4+ years as an architect leading Microsoft-based transformation or migration programs.
  • US citizenship required.
  • Deep expertise in Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, and Windows Server.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft 365 workloads and migration tooling.
  • Experience with Microsoft Intune and Configuration Manager.
  • Working knowledge of federal security and compliance frameworks, including NIST RMF, FISMA, FedRAMP, and DISA STIGs.
  • Strong PowerShell scripting and Infrastructure as Code skills.

raw.description:
Financial Data Manager

Counterpart is the first Agentic Insurance™ platform, combining trusted insurance expertise with cutting-edge AI to deliver tailored management and professional liability solutions. By integrating Agentic Underwriting™, Agentic Broker Services™, Agentic Risk Mitigation™, Agentic Claims Management™, Agentic Coverage™, and Agentic Capacity™ into one powerful platform, Counterpart empowers brokers - and the businesses they serve - to do more with less risk. Backed by A rated carriers, Counterpart has been recognized by CB Insights as a 2025 “Top 50 Insurtech,” by Great Place to Work, and by Business Insurance as one of its 2025 “Best Places to Work.”

We're seeking a Financial Data Manager to design and deliver the data workflows that power Counterpart's financial and accounting systems. You will report to Pricing & Analytics and serve three primary customers: the finance function, the analytics function, and broker services (billing). You will translate insurance accounting concepts — written and earned premium, unearned premium reserves, commissions, and cash application — into clear data requirements. You will then partner with engineering to build them. This is a design and project management role at the intersection of finance, data, and product.

YOU WILL

  • Design data-driven workflows that feed Counterpart's financial and accounting systems and the downstream processes that depend on them.
  • Translate finance, analytics, and billing requirements into clear data models, source-of-truth definitions, and technical specifications.
  • Own the definitions behind core insurance accounting measures — written premium, earned premium, unearned premium, commissions, and ceded amounts — so every team reports the same number.
  • Partner with engineering to implement these workflows, and manage the projects end to end from scoping through delivery and adoption. Enable resilient systems that can handle edge cases (even with easy manual override)
  • Serve as the primary data partner to the finance function for the monthly and quarterly close, reconciliations, and audit support.
  • Support broker services on billing and invoicing data, including installment schedules, cash application, and commission accuracy.
  • Build controls and automated checks that catch premium, billing, and bordereau discrepancies before they reach carriers or auditors.
  • Design and maintain the carrier and bordereau reporting pipelines, and make sure the outputs tie to the general ledger.
  • Document data lineage, change tracking, business rules, and known limitations so finance and analytics users can self-serve with confidence.
  • Prioritize a backlog of finance data requests, and set expectations with stakeholders on scope, sequence, and timing.
  • Identify manual finance processes that data and automation can remove, and build the business case to fix them.

YOU HAVE

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, economics, information systems, or a related field.
  • 5+ years in financial data management, financial systems, insurance operations, or a comparable analytical role.
  • A working knowledge of insurance accounting concepts, including written premium, earned premium, unearned premium reserves, and commissions.
  • Practical SQL skills — you can query, join, and validate data on your own without waiting on an analyst.
  • Experience writing requirements for engineering teams and managing delivery against them.
  • Strong project management skills, and a track record of shipping cross-functional work with finance and technical partners.
  • Clear written communication, and the ability to explain data decisions to accountants and engineers alike.
  • Experience with data warehouses and business intelligence tools (Snowflake, Looker, dbt, or similar) is a plus.
  • Insurance, insurtech, or fintech experience is highly desirable.

WHO YOU WILL WORK WITH:

  • Stanley Wang, Director, Pricing Analytics: Before joining Counterpart, Stanley worked as an actuary within the pricing solutions and methods team at USAA to combine actuarial pricing with data science models. Before that, he was a leading data scientist for Digital Partners, a Munich Re Company where he specialized in building data science models and insights for leading insurtech companies. He has had many other relevant roles such as capital modeling, risk management etc. He lives in New York with his growing family.
  • Tobias Schuler, Chief Underwriting Officer: After becoming a Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society & working as a consultant actuary at EY for several years, Tobias went on to drive the actuarial data & systems teams at QBE. He further leveraged his deep insurance & technical expertise at Munich Re Digital Partners in North America, where he headed data & analytics & oversaw the data infrastructure behind some of their largest programs.
  • Newton Truong, Engineering Manager: Newton joins Counterpart with 7+ years of experience in platform and data engineering. In his last company Thrive Market, he had a hand in building out new microservices and architecting data pipelines with Airflow and Spark. He's vegetarian and loves trying new restaurants when traveling. Nowadays he's busy keeping up with his 2-year-old and doing outdoor activities with his family.

COUNTERPART'S VALUES

  • Conjoin Expectations - it is the cornerstone of autonomy. Ensure you are aware of what is expected of you and clearly articulate what you expect of others.
  • Speak Boldly & Honestly - the only failure is not learning from mistakes. Don't cheat yourself and your colleagues of the feedback needed when expectations aren't being met.
  • Be Entrepreneurial - control your own destiny. Embrace action over perfection while navigating any obstacles that stand in the way of your ultimate goal. Leverage AI ruthlessly. We measure success by outcomes, not lines of code written. Use every available AI tool to ship faster and think more strategically.
  • Practice Omotenashi ("selfless hospitality") - trust will follow. Consider every interaction with internal and external partners an opportunity to develop trust by going above and beyond what is expected.
  • Hold Nothing As Sacred - create routines but modify them routinely. Take the time to reflect on where the business is today, where it needs to go, and what you have to change in order to get there.
  • Prioritize Wellness - some things should never be sacrificed. We create an environment that stretches everyone to grow and improve, which is fulfilling, but is only one part of a meaningful life.

WE OFFER

  • Fully remote workplace
  • Unlimited Vacation: We offer flexible time off, allowing you to take time when you need it.
  • Work from Anywhere: Counterpart is a fully distributed company, meaning there is no office. We allow employees to work from wherever they do their best work, and invite the team to meet in person a couple times per year.
  • Stock Options
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Coverage
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan
  • Parental Leave
  • Home Office Allowance: to set up your home office with the necessary equipment and accessories.
  • Wellness Stipend
  • Book stipend
  • Professional Development Reimbursement
  • No working birthdays: Take your birthday off, giving you the opportunity to relax, enjoy your special day, and spend time with loved ones.
  • Charitable Contribution Matching

Our estimated pay range for this role is $150,000 to $180,000. Base salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, market data, location, internal equitability, and experience.

We are committed to being a welcoming and inclusive workplace for everyone, and we are intentional about making sure people feel respected, supported and connected at work - regardless of who you are or where you come from. We value and celebrate our differences and we believe being open about who we are allows us to do the best work of our lives.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate against qualified applicants or employees on the basis of race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, sexual preference, sexual identity, pregnancy, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, marital status, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, military status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law, rule, or regulation.

Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As a Critical Account Lead, you will serve as the single point of accountability for Baxter's most complex customer escalations within the Care Communications Solutions business. This newly created role was designed to improve the customer experience when issues span multiple products, teams, or technologies.


You'll partner closely with Technical Support, Product Management, R&D, Customer Success, Sales, and leadership teams to coordinate resolution efforts and ensure customers have a clear path forward. This is an opportunity to help build a new function, influence how critical customer situations are managed, and play a direct role in strengthening Baxter's relationships with healthcare customers.


What You'll Do

  • Own critical customer escalations from intake through customer stabilization, serving as the single point of accountability throughout the lifecycle.
  • Triage incoming escalations, assess severity levels, and determine appropriate engagement and response plans.
  • Lead cross-functional resolution teams across Technical Support, Product Management, R&D, Customer Success, Services, and Sales.
  • Coordinate resolution activities for complex customer issues, including incidents that span multiple products, technologies, business units, and support organizations.
  • Deliver executive-level status updates and escalation communications to internal stakeholders and customer leadership.
  • Maintain escalation records, action plans, and status reporting within established systems and processes.
  • Conduct post-incident reviews, document root causes, and identify opportunities to improve products, processes, and customer outcomes.
  • Support the development of escalation criteria, critical account pathways, performance metrics, and scalable operational processes for the Critical Account Lead program.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Healthcare, Information Technology, Business, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in technical support, escalation management, technical account management, customer success, program management, or related customer-facing technical roles.
  • Experience managing high-severity customer issues that require coordination across multiple teams, products, or business functions.
  • Knowledge of healthcare technology environments, hospital IT operations, or medical device technologies.
  • Experience working with networking technologies and HL7 integrations.

The Senior Director, Clinical Research - Infusion Therapies & Technologies serves as the scientific leader responsible for transforming medical, clinical, and business priorities into executable evidence-generation strategies across Baxter's ITP portfolio, including pharmaceuticals, nutrition therapies, infusion systems, pharmacy technologies, and medication delivery solutions.

Working in close partnership with Medical Affairs, the Senior Director translates unmet medical needs and strategic evidence priorities into scientifically rigorous research programs capable of generating meaningful clinical, economic, and operational evidence to support innovation, product development, regulatory submissions, post-market evidence generation, clinical practice adoption, and value-based healthcare initiatives. The role provides leadership in study methodology, evidence strategy, research governance, scientific interpretation, and cross-functional execution.

The Senior Director works with Medical Affairs and Clinical Operations, ensuring that research programs are scientifically sound, operationally feasible, aligned with regulatory expectations, and capable of generating evidence that advances patient care and business objectives.

What you'll be doing:

Clinical Research Strategy & Evidence Planning

  • Partner with Medical Affairs to convert medical evidence priorities into integrated clinical research strategies.
  • Design evidence-generation programs that address unmet clinical, scientific, healthcare system, and customer needs.
  • Develop fit-for-purpose study designs.
  • Establish research plans that generate evidence relevant to clinicians, regulators, payers, providers, and healthcare systems.

Scientific Leadership

  • Serve as the organization's leading expert in clinical research methodology and scientific study design.
  • Ensure appropriate application of epidemiology, biostatistics, implementation science, health-services research, and clinical study methodologies.
  • Provide scientific oversight for protocols, statistical plans, clinical study reports, and evidence interpretation.
  • Ensure scientific rigor across all clinical research activities.

Clinical Operations Leadership

  • Lead the Clinical Operations team and partner with them to optimize feasibility, execution quality, enrollment strategies, and study delivery.
  • Ensure study designs appropriately balance scientific rigor, operational feasibility, project timelines, and resource requirements.
  • Participate in governance and risk mitigation activities for ongoing studies.
  • Support study execution through interpretation of emerging data and resolution of scientific issues.

  • Advanced scientific or clinical degree (MD, PharmD, PhD, DNP, or equivalent).
  • Minimum 10 years of experience in clinical research, clinical development, medical affairs, or evidence generation.
  • Experience leading development and execution of clinical studies and evidence-generation programs.
  • Experience working within regulated healthcare environments.
  • Strong understanding of GCP, global regulatory expectations, and evidence-generation requirements.
  • Experience generating evidence across multiple evidence domains, including clinical outcomes, safety, workflow efficiency, human factors, usability, implementation science, real-world evidence, and health economic outcomes.
  • Builds trusted partnerships across Medical Affairs, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, R&D, HEOR, Commercial, and Quality.
  • Aligns diverse stakeholders around a common research vision.
  • Applies deep understanding of clinical research methodology to complex scientific and business questions.
  • Designs innovative evidence-generation approaches across pharmaceuticals, devices, and healthcare technologies.
  • Adapts rapidly to evolving portfolio priorities.
  • Effectively operates in ambiguity and changing business environments.
  • Demonstrates an entrepreneurial mindset.
  • Comfortable building new capabilities and processes.
  • Bias toward action and execution.
  • Challenges traditional approaches to accelerate learning and impact.
  • Balances innovation with scientific rigor.
  • Willingness to travel approximately 25% of the time.
  • Strong business acumen and impeccable integrity.

raw.description:
This is where your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your role at Baxter


As a Senior AI Security Architect, you will play a key role in helping Baxter securely adopt and scale Artificial Intelligence technologies across the enterprise. This position sits within Baxter's Cybersecurity organization and serves as the primary security expert for AI technologies, including Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), AI Agents, and machine learning platforms.


You will partner closely with teams across Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, Data & Analytics, Infrastructure, R&D, Privacy, Legal, and Quality to establish the security standards, governance frameworks, and guardrails needed to enable responsible AI innovation. As Baxter continues to expand the use of AI across products, operations, and corporate functions, you will help shape the company's AI security strategy while balancing innovation, risk management, and regulatory requirements.


This is an opportunity to join Baxter early in its AI journey and help define how AI technologies are secured across a global healthcare organization. The role offers significant visibility, cross-functional exposure, and the opportunity to grow into a broader cybersecurity leadership role over time.


This is a remote U.S.-based role with quarterly travel to Baxter's Deerfield, IL headquarters.


What you'll be doing


  • Lead security reviews and assessments for AI, Generative AI, machine learning, and AI agent solutions across the enterprise.
  • Define AI security standards, architectures, and best practices that support secure and responsible AI adoption.
  • Partner with technical and business teams to evaluate new AI technologies, platforms, vendors, and use cases from a security and risk perspective.
  • Conduct threat modeling, architecture reviews, and risk assessments for AI applications and platforms.
  • Establish security controls and guardrails for LLMs, AI copilots, RAG solutions, AI agents, and related technologies.
  • Support AI governance initiatives by defining security requirements, approval processes, monitoring capabilities, and risk management practices.
  • Collaborate with Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, Data & Analytics, R&D, Privacy, Legal, and Quality teams to ensure AI solutions meet security and compliance requirements.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor and mentor to architects, engineers, developers, and business stakeholders on AI security best practices.

What you'll bring


  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in cybersecurity, security architecture, enterprise architecture, or related technology disciplines.
  • Experience securing AI, Generative AI, machine learning, cloud, or advanced analytics environments.
  • Strong understanding of AI security risks, including prompt injection, data leakage, model poisoning, adversarial attacks, and unauthorized model access.
  • Hands-on experience with AI platforms such as Microsoft Copilot, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Services, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or similar technologies.
  • Experience conducting threat modeling, security architecture reviews, and enterprise risk assessments.
  • Knowledge of identity and access management, cloud security, data protection, encryption, API security, and AI governance principles.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder management, and executive presentation skills, with the ability to influence across a complex global organization.

Nice to Have


  • Experience with Microsoft security technologies including Purview, Defender, Entra ID, and Azure security services.
  • Familiarity with AI governance frameworks such as NIST AI RMF, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 42001, or ISO 27001.
  • Experience working in regulated industries such as healthcare, medical device, manufacturing, automotive, or other environments with significant compliance requirements.
  • Professional certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, Azure Security Engineer, Azure Solutions Architect, or similar credentials.

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. At Baxter, we are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. The estimated base salary for this position is $152,000 - $209,000. The estimated range is meant to reflect an anticipated salary range for the position. We may pay more or less than of the anticipated range based upon market data and other factors, all of which are subject to change. Individual pay is based on upon location, skills and expertise, experience, and other relevant factors. This position is also eligible for discretionary bonuses. For questions about this, our pay philosophy, and available benefits, please speak to the recruiter if you decide to apply and are selected for an interview.


Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

US Benefits at Baxter (except for Puerto Rico)

This is where your well-being matters. Baxter offers comprehensive compensation and benefits packages for eligible roles. Our health and well-being benefits include medical and dental coverage that start on day one, as well as insurance coverage for basic life, accident, short-term and long-term disability, and business travel accident insurance. Financial and retirement benefits include the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), with the ability to purchase company stock at a discount, and the 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan (RSP), with options for employee contributions and company matching. We also offer Flexible Spending Accounts, educational assistance programs, and time-off benefits such as paid holidays, paid time off ranging from 20 to 35 days based on length of service, family and medical leaves of absence, and paid parental leave. Additional benefits include commuting benefits, the Employee Discount Program, the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and childcare benefits. Join us and enjoy the competitive compensation and benefits we offer to our employees. For additional information regarding Baxter US Benefits, please speak with your recruiter or visit our Benefits site: Benefits | Baxter

Baxter is an equal opportunity employer. Baxter evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, protected veteran status, disability/handicap status or any other legally protected characteristic.

Job Description:

GDIT is the leading systems integrator in the Zero Trust Defense sector market—developing and delivering innovative solutions to government customers. Our Zero Trust business continues experiencing rapid growth, and this is an opportunity to join our team and be a part of creating Cybersecurity solutions that make a real impact.

As a Cyber Security Architect on an Enterprise Zero Trust Program for a DoD client, your responsibilities will include:

  • Develop and implement long-term cybersecurity strategies and plans, ensuring alignment with business goals and regulatory requirements.

  • Leading RMF efforts for a large distributed system in order to obtain an ATO

  • Identify, analyze, and assess security risks, developing and implementing mitigation strategies.

  • Create and enforce security policies, procedures, and guidelines to ensure compliance and maintain a secure environment.

  • Support incident response efforts, including detection, containment, eradication, and recovery, in the event of security breaches or incidents.

  • Support vulnerability assessments, penetration testing, and other security tests to identify weaknesses and vulnerabilities in systems and networks.

  • Collaborate with other IT professionals, business stakeholders, and external vendors to ensure security requirements are met.

  • Remain up to date on the latest cybersecurity threats, technologies, and best practices.

  • Provide guidance and mentoring to junior security professionals and trains employees on security best practices.

  • Interface with government customer to present program cyber risks.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Understanding of security principles involved in Zero Trust Network Architecture and tools required to implement it

  • Understanding of how networks function, including protocols, devices, and security measures like firewalls and VLANs.

  • Knowledge of data protection methods, including encryption, pseudonymization, and data masking.

  • Understanding of risk assessment, analysis, and mitigation techniques.

  • Skills in identifying, analyzing, and responding to security incidents.

  • Ability to analyze problems, troubleshoot security issues, and develop effective solutions.

  • Capacity to learn and adapt to new technologies and evolving threats.

  • Ability to clearly explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Ability to work effectively with other teams and stakeholders.

  • Detail oriented.

Required Skills/Knowledge:

  • 5-10 years of experience in IT security and IT risk management is recommended.

  • Current Secret clearance.

  • DoD 8570 IAT Level III certification.

  • Advanced IT security certifications (like CISSP, CEH, GIAC).

  • Bachelor’s degree in field like Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

  • Strong foundation in information security frameworks and IT risk management practices.

  • Expertise in DoD RMF Controls and how to correlate the various aspects of the systems, networks, and applications to ensure controls are closed and/or mitigated, and documented in furtherance of obtaining ATO

  • Expertise in security audits, compliance requirements, and regulatory standards.

  • Deep understanding of enterprise architecture principles and how to integrate security into the overall IT landscape.

  • Knowledge of secure coding practices, vulnerability assessment, and penetration testing.

  • Knowledge of common operating systems (Windows, Linux, Unix) and their security configurations.

  • Proficiency in various zero trust security tools and technologies, such as intrusion detection systems, data loss prevention (DLP) solutions, identity and access management (IAM) systems, firewalls, and ZTNA.

GDIT IS YOUR PLACE:

  • Full-flex work week to own your priorities at work and at home

  • 401K with company match

  • Comprehensive health and wellness packages

  • Internal mobility team dedicated to helping you own your career

  • Professional growth opportunities including paid education and certifications

  • Cutting-edge technology you can learn from

  • Rest and recharge with paid vacation and holidays

The likely salary range for this position is $149,469 - $184,000. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. Rather, salary will be set based on experience, geographic location and possibly contractual requirements and could fall outside of this range.

Our benefits package for all US-based employees includes a variety of medical plan options, some with Health Savings Accounts, dental plan options, a vision plan, and a 401(k) plan offering the ability to contribute both pre and post-tax dollars up to the IRS annual limits and receive a company match. To encourage work/life balance, GDIT offers employees full flex work weeks where possible and a variety of paid time off plans, including vacation, sick and personal time, holidays, paid parental, military, bereavement and jury duty leave. GDIT typically provides new employees with 15 days of paid leave per calendar year to be used for vacations, personal business, and illness and an additional 10 paid holidays per year. Paid leave and paid holidays are prorated based on the employee’s date of hire. The GDIT Paid Family Leave program provides a total of up to 160 hours of paid leave in a rolling 12 month period for eligible employees. To ensure our employees are able to protect their income, other offerings such as short and long-term disability benefits, life, accidental death and dismemberment, personal accident, critical illness and business travel and accident insurance are provided or available. We regularly review our Total Rewards package to ensure our offerings are competitive and reflect what our employees have told us they value most.

Our Identity Verification Process:

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during virtual interviews. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. By proceeding, you authorize the collection, processing, and use of your biometric data for identity verification and security purposes.

We are GDIT. Our 26,000 experts extract the power of technology to create immediate value and deliver solutions at the edge of innovation. About this role:
Our Chief HR Officer clients find themselves challenged with the pace of change within the HR function and their respective organizations as companies continue to focus on developing digital dexterity, shifting business models and evolving customer and workforce expectations. With the support of their Executive Partner, our Gartner for CHRO clients adeptly assess the changes needed within their organization, achieve their goals more quickly and with a higher assurance of success. As an Executive Partner, you will have the opportunity to learn about and deliver solutions for the most complex talent and workforce challenges facing companies across all industries.

Partnering with the member includes developing, coaching and/or critiquing overarching HR and talent strategies; helping to develop and/or transform their HR teams/organizations, assisting/advising with the development and execution of critical initiatives such as workforce planning and development, employee experience, enterprise change management, and diversity and inclusion. Gartner for CHRO Executive Partners serve as accountability partners through delivery of research insights and personal experiences/expertise on key initiatives, priorities, and strategies.

What You’ll Do:

  • Provide executive advisory services to approximately 20 CHRO members who work across all industries and business models.
  • Work as a collaborative Gartner team member serving Gartner for CHRO members in conjunction with Team Client Managers and Account Executives
  • Participate in all phases of the member lifecycle: pre-sale, on-boarding, relationship management, delivery, review and renewal.
  • Responsible for member retention and for contributing toward growth in the region through direct support of Gartner Sales in prospect cultivation, account plan development and value demonstration activities.
  • Host and /or participate in periodic member activities, including strategy workshops, roundtables and webinars.
  • Define and deliver innovative solutions by assessing member needs and developing a customized value plan in accordance with overall Executive Program strategy and product deliverables.
  • Facilitate member interaction and peer collaboration through the Gartner for CHRO member community portal and assisted member connections.

What You’ll Need:

  • An undergraduate degree or Masters is preferred with 5+ years of experience working as a CHRO; 15+ years of experience in HR.
  • An in-depth understanding of the HR function and the role of the CHRO (including leadership, operations management, strategy and trends, use of metrics, etc.)
  • In depth understanding of the business value of HR and the alignment of business and HR strategies.
  • The Executive Partner will be an accomplished CHRO, working with the C-suite, the Board of Directors and a host of stakeholders with a broad base of expertise who has operated at a senior leadership level and driven change at all levels.
  • Gartner/(CEB) client experience preferred
  • Consulting background a plus
  • Experience consulting into the federal government on human capital issues is a plus

Who You Are:

  • Critical thinker and problem solver demonstrating the ability to assess our Member’s situations and provide actionable, outcome-based business/technical advice as well as the ability to leverage appropriate resources to help Members achieve results.
  • Excellent communication and relationship management skills, including experience working with C-level executives.
  • Ability to build strategic internal partnerships with key roles across the organization and positively impact change
  • This role is a Client-facing position that requires a high level of Executive presence and ability to quickly build trust and deliver value.
  • Demonstrate superior verbal and written communication skills as well as strong facilitation and presentation skills.

THIS IS A REMOTE POSITION THAT CAN BE LOCATED ANYWHERE IN THE UNITED STATES.

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 188,000 USD - 225,000 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location. In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based, uncapped sales incentive plan. Our talent acquisition team will provide the specific opportunity on our bonus or incentive programs to eligible candidates. We also offer market leading benefit programs including generous PTO, a 401k match up to $7,200 per year, the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount, and more.

The policy of Gartner is to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, citizenship status, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status and to seek to advance the principles of equal employment opportunity.

Gartner is committed to being an Equal Opportunity Employer and offers opportunities to all job seekers, including job seekers with disabilities. If you are a qualified individual with a disability or a disabled veteran, you may request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access the Company’s career webpage as a result of your disability. Turn complexity into clarity and deliver innovative applications as a Project Manager - Scrum Master supporting a Program Management Office (PMO) on a large, complex Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) contract. GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career.

Here, you’ll support our customers’ most important missions with smart, scalable solutions while we support you in growing and developing your technology career.

HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:

  • Foster a collaborative, high-energy team environment focused on delivering high-value solutions
  • Drive effective sprint execution by ensuring clear priorities, strong team alignment, and disciplined Agile practices
  • Enhance transparency and accountability through accurate documentation of sprint plans, release plans, team agreements, and retrospectives

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As a Clinical Integration Specialist, you will be responsible for providing clinical and technical expertise, best-practice standards, and professional skills to support Sales and Services engagements for the Baxter Care Communications product portfolio of Digital Health products.


You will report to the Clinical Integrations Manager, will work internally in close partnership with Sales, Clinical Solutions, Project Managers, and Services and Support, and will work with customer clinical and technical staff to design and implement solutions.

  • TRAVEL: Up to 80% travel, including overnight travel. 100% REMOTE

Your Team

We embrace opportunities to connect with the doctors, nurses, and other healthcare professionals that use our products every day to save and sustain lives. Observing their work, understanding their needs, and building positive relationships are integral to our success.


What you'll be doing

  • Collaborate with team members to architect accurate clinical assessment documents for customer-facing integration, alarm management middleware, and nurse call engagements
  • Consult on and configure alarm management middleware settings and nurse call configurations based on the clinical design workbook
  • Manage multiple, simultaneous projects from assessment through implementation for clinical integration consulting programs
  • Interface at all levels within a customer's organization and coordinate technical information and healthcare ecosystem requirements
  • Assist other team members with tasks required to execute delivery of clinical integration consulting programs
  • Aid in mentorship, continuous skill building and onboarding activities within Clinical Operations
  • Interact daily with customers through in-person, phone, and web conference activities
  • Provide input to product management, market planning, and technical development of Clinical Solutions
  • Incorporate quality and continuous improvement as part of overall job performance; adhering and training to Bater's QMS policies and procedures
  • Maintain up-to-date understanding of healthcare trends and technical developments

What you'll bring

  • Degree/certification in Business, IT, Project Management, Clinical Informatics, or related experience
  • Clinical experience in acute care hospital environment preferred
  • Ability to articulate, design, and successfully implement clinical technology
  • Facilitate change management philosophies to enhance the adoption of all Baxter Care Communication programs
  • Excellent written and verbal presentation skills and ability to build written content with little direction
  • Experience with Microsoft Office suite
  • Must be able to work in team environment or independently making clinical consulting decisions without guidance
  • Strong conflict resolution skills, including the abilities to negotiate and influence others
  • Good problem solving and analytical skills to understand key customer clinical issues and define how IT solutions will solve challenges facing our customers today
  • Experience with standards development based on healthcare industry trends
  • Ability to react to changes in priorities, demands, timelines, and scope promptly and efficiently, through analytical and problem-solving techniques
  • Ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment
  • Customer minded - actively evaluate and work to improve the customer experience

raw.description:
What You'll Do


  • Serve as a trusted advisor to Chief Marketing Officers and senior marketing leaders across Gartner's enterprise client base.
  • Deliver one-on-one executive guidance aligned to each leader's strategic priorities, organizational challenges, and business objectives.
  • Advise marketing executives on areas including:
  • Marketing strategy and transformation

  • Demand generation and pipeline acceleration

- Brand strategy and positioning

- Customer acquisition and retention

  • Customer experience and journey optimization
  • Marketing technology and digital transformation

- AI-enabled marketing capabilities

  • Marketing operating models and organizational design
  • Board and CEO stakeholder management
  • Facilitate executive-level discussions, workshops, and peer forums that help CMOs learn from one another and exchange best practices.
  • Leverage Gartner research and proprietary insights to enhance executive decision-making.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior leaders and become a valued extension of their leadership team.
  • Identify emerging trends, risks, and opportunities shaping the future of marketing leadership.

Who You Are


  • You are a former senior marketing executive who has successfully led marketing organizations in complex, high-growth, and large-scale enterprises (≥$1B).
  • You possess the executive presence, strategic perspective, and business acumen required to engage with CMOs as a true peer.
  • You are equally comfortable discussing enterprise growth strategy, board-level expectations, brand and demand generation, marketing technology, and organizational leadership. Most importantly, you have a passion for helping other executives succeed.

Required Experience


  • 15+ years of progressive marketing leadership experience.
  • Significant experience serving in a senior marketing leadership role, preferably as: Chief Marketing Officer, SVP Marketing, EVP Marketing, Chief Growth Officer, Chief Customer Officer
  • Experience leading marketing functions within rapidly scaling enterprise organizations operating at ≥$1B in annual revenue
  • Demonstrated ownership of enterprise marketing strategy and business outcomes.
  • Experience partnering directly with CEOs, Boards of Directors, executive leadership teams, and revenue-generating business units.
  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive organizational change.
  • Strong executive communication, coaching, and relationship-building skills.

Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience in B2C, professional services, or global organizations.
  • Experience overseeing substantial marketing budgets and cross-functional teams.
  • Background in modern marketing disciplines, including digital marketing, customer experience, marketing analytics, AI-enabled marketing, and revenue marketing.
  • Prior experience advising, coaching, mentoring, or developing senior executives.

What Makes This Opportunity Unique


  • Engage with CMOs from some of the world's most recognized organizations.
  • Influence strategic decisions across multiple industries rather than a single company.
  • Join an elite network of former executives and thought leaders.
  • Leverage Gartner's world-class research and intellectual capital to help clients make confident decisions.
  • Continue shaping the future of business and marketing leadership without returning to an operational role.

📍Remote - United States

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 188,000 USD - 225,000 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location. In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based, uncapped sales incentive plan. Our talent acquisition team will provide the specific opportunity on our bonus or incentive programs to eligible candidates. Adjunct Faculty – Artificial Intelligence (BS Program)

Department of Information Technology | University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC)

This position is specifically to teach remotely for stateside applicants. Local applicants only; UMGC does not sponsor logistical support for this role.

At UMGC, we don’t just teach; we empower. Founded in 1947, UMGC is an open-access, minority-serving institution serving over 90,000 nontraditional learners worldwide, including a proud, large military-affiliated population. Our students are mature, highly dedicated, and balancing careers, families, and service. As an Adjunct Faculty member, you are the essential partner helping them bridge the gap between classroom theory and real-world career success.

Why Teach with UMGC?

  • Focus on Students, Not Course Design: All courses follow a standardized, pre-designed, unified course model. Standardized rubrics, OER materials, library resources, and digital textbooks are fully provided at no cost to you. You get to focus 100% of your energy on mentoring, facilitating, and providing high-quality feedback—no unpaid course-building required.
  • True Asynchronous Flexibility: Teach with flexibility, on your own schedule. As long as you meet weekly grading, responsiveness, and engagement milestones, your daily hours are entirely up to you.
  • Ongoing Growth: We invest in you. All newly hired faculty receive comprehensive online orientation, alongside ongoing, cost-free professional development opportunities.

The Rhythm of Your Week (Key Responsibilities)

Adjunct faculty bring our pre-built curriculum to life through real-world expertise and active mentorship.

Classroom Engagement & Presence

  • Be Visible: Maintain an active classroom presence at least 5 days per week, introducing yourself with a welcome announcement and driving discussions.
  • Bridge Theory & Practice: Enrich the pre-built curriculum with your own professional expertise and real-world examples.
  • Build Belonging: Foster an inclusive, culturally responsive environment where adult learners feel supported and motivated.

Responsiveness & Feedback

  • Stay consistently engaged with learners throughout the course by responding to inquiries, returning feedback, and posting final grades within the expected timeframe.

Proactive Support & Collaboration

  • Monitor Progress: Use available data tools to track student engagement and conduct proactive outreach to at-risk students.
  • Team Up: Partner with success coaches, academic staff, and portfolio directors to refer struggling students to UMGC support resources.
  • Stay Connected: Participate in UMGC's vibrant faculty community, including the Program Hub and ongoing training.

Course Structure & Time Commitment

  • Format: 100% Online & Asynchronous

  • Class Size: Typically, 25–35 students (smaller sections for select courses)

raw.excerpt: Compensation Range: Annual Salary: $66,560. 00 - $75,066.
raw.description:
Compensation Range:

Annual Salary: $66,560.00 - $75,066.00

National University – San Diego, California

Assistant Professor in Clinical Mental Health – Remote, USA

The Department of Counseling Psychology and Social Work, in the John F. Kennedy School of Psychology and Social Sciences at National University, invites applications for an Assistant Professor in the Clinical Mental Health program. Rank is commensurate with qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will have the potential for excellence in teaching and scholarship in the counseling field and a commitment to serving the university’s diverse adult student body. This position is remote. This position works closely with other faculty within the discipline and administration contributing to programmatic strategies that ensure program quality, student engagement, and success. We are looking for a candidate who can collaborate with faculty, program leadership, and operations staff to support the delivery of comprehensive, high-quality academic and clinical training experience for students. While the primary function of this role is teaching and requires the ability to teach across various courses, it also integrates service, scholarship, and clinical training experience to support student development and program excellence. The Assistant Professor reports to the Department Chair and works closely with CMHC leadership to ensure alignment with programmatic goals and accreditation standards, including those established by CACREP.

Essential Functions

Candidates will be evaluated for their level of proficiency and potential (for excellence) in teaching, scholarship, and service. The main expectations of this position include:

Teaching

  • Teach and develop online courses in the area of clinical mental health in content areas of counseling theories, assessment and testing, and diagnosis and treatment.
  • Teach clinical courses and participate in Final Presentations.
  • Maintain pedagogical and subject matter expertise in the instructor’s field.
  • Create an inclusive and positive learning environment for diverse learners.
  • Ensure course and program practices align with compliance and accreditation standards.
  • Adhere to the National University’s academic integrity policy.

Scholarship

  • Maintain a productive scholarship agenda suitable to a teaching university.
  • Engage in scholarly activities to maintain professional growth with counseling organizations such as the American Counseling Association.
  • Participate in professional development as outlined in faculty policies.

Service

  • Support school and program leadership on accreditation reviews.
  • Consult on program processes and participate in discussions to improve and innovate the CMHC program.
  • Provide regular opportunities to offer academic guidance and mentorship to individual CMHC students on training process and placements, program requirements, development of practicum and career goals, and any problems/concerns that they encounter throughout the tenor of their program.
  • Participates in any remediation processes involving CMHC students.
  • Serve as a reviewer of all program materials to ensure compliance with CACREP and state standards.
  • Collaborate and provide support to internal stakeholders on appropriate data collection, analysis, evaluation, and dissemination of reports including the regular evaluation of the students’ comportment and experience quality.
  • Serve a faculty advisor for student organizations such as CSI and faculty point of contact for student programming such as new student orientation, graduation celebration, etc.
  • Maintain professional communication with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Participate in administrative meetings and project teams as requested.
  • Complete all other tasks and/or projects as assigned.
  • Maintain membership and actively participate with professional counseling organizations such as the American Counseling Association.

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications:

Education & Experience

  • Doctoral degree in Counselor Education and Supervision from a CACREP-accredited institution/program required.
  • Licensed or license eligible as a professional counselor (LPC) required.
  • Strong identification with professional counselor identity and evidence of such, e.g., membership in professional counselor organization(s), licensing activities, conference attendance, etc., required.
  • 2+ years of faculty experience in a program in a CACREP accredited CMHC program and/or clinical training administration experience in a CACREP accredited CMHC program preferred.
  • Experience with CACREP accreditation and compliance as well as ability to assist in management of such preferred
  • Experience teaching online courses in asynchronous format; experience working in a technology-driven enterprise preferred.
  • Curriculum development experience preferred.

Special conditions of employment include:

  • Background check required.
  • Travel is required at least once annually to attend the annual Commencement ceremony (if held onsite).

For full consideration, interested candidates should provide the following:

  • A cover letter that includes interest in the position and brief summary of required qualifications met.
  • A curriculum vita
  • Statement of teaching experience online and/or onsite for a diverse student body.

Candidate receiving offers will be offered a salary/pay rate commensurate with experience that vary based on a candidate’s qualifications, skills, and competencies. Absent exceptional circumstances, candidates will be offered a salary within this range for this position. Base pay is one component of National University’s total rewards package, as we are dedicated to supporting the needs of the “whole you” with our holistic approach to employee benefits by offering comprehensive well-being benefits for you and your family. For full details about our benefit plan offerings, please visit . For part-time positions, please click here.

National University is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant per applicable federal, state and local laws. At NU, a mix of highly talented, innovative, and creative people come together to make the impact of a lifetime for each of our student learners. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment, education, and admission at National University.
